$BTC 200 Week Moving Average Heatmap is based on the percentage increases of the Weekly 200MA.

If it's increasing a lot, due to explosive price action towards the upside, you'll see warmer colors.

These colors are generally also close to a top while the colder colors are generally seen during the bottom & mid cycles.

Good to note that price action will generally be slower over time as BTC has grown and the market matured.

$BTC Generally offers good buying opportunities when it's trading at/below its 2 year moving average.

A tool for determining previous cycle tops has been to take the 2 year moving average and multiply it by 5.

This marked the 2021 cycle top nicely. In the 2013 & 2017 cycles, price even traded above it.

While I think it's unlikely for BTC to reach this level again due to it's size and the market maturing, I think it can still be a decent tool to watch.

Still gives a good idea of where BTC is trading relative to the high timeframe extremes.

Often, the moment you feel like giving up on your coins is the moment you should actually be buying and vice versa.

The best long term buys I've done are the ones I did while feeling sick in my stomach from all the pain we endured the weeks/months before.

On the other side, the worst buys are generally the ones where you feel you don't own enough after prices have already gone up a lot.

About Large Token Unlocks 📚

Large token unlocks are a bit difficult to navigate as price action into and after the event, can vary greatly.

On one hand, the unlock is known in advance, there's usually OTC sales before and also a lot of hedging  (which unwinds after). The latter also causes funding rates to go deeply into the negative which means shorts are paying a hefty premium to keep their positions open.

On the other hand, it is still a large unlock and can sometimes account for a 100%+ supply increase. So even if a relatively small part of the tokens get sold on the open market, it will weigh down on price.

Generally speaking, what happens is very market and team/investor dependent.

Some teams/investors opt to extend the unlock or have put in measures (by selling OTC against a discount with a vesting attached) to limit the potential selling when the unlock occurs. This spreads out the potential supply hitting the market over a longer period of time to help absorb the selling.

Also, when the market is going ballistic and everything is pumping, these unlocks usually just tend to squeeze out the shorts that have piled in and the actual selling doesn't come until the market has cooled off.

So there's no easy approach here, it's dependent on multiple variables. Usually people trying to trade it get chopped up or eat a lot of funding rates when doing so. I've tried trading these in previous years with varied results. But have found no clear edge personally.
